summary: Raghu Vira was an Indology, Iranian, and Central Asian Buddhist studies scholar. He earned degrees at Punjab, London, and Leiden. He served as Sanskrit Department Head at Sanatan Dharma College (~1928–1934) and Director of the International Academy of Indian Culture from 1934.

Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Ex-Principal of Sir Parashurambhau College (attested 1970) and worked at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, including as Department Director (attested 1953) and Professor (attested 1966).
Raghunath Giri was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya and held a post as department head (科長) at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Rahul Peter Das is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler, completing his degrees at Hamburg. He researched and taught at Hamburg, Bonn, and Groningen before becoming Professor at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1994–2020).

Rahul Sankrityayan worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He taught Sanskrit at Vidyalankara Pirivena (1927) and later served at the University of Saint Petersburg as a Sanskrit teacher (1937) and professor (1945–1947).

Raimo Anttila was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied under Warren Cowgill at Yale University (~1962–1966). He held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles (1965) and the University of Helsinki (1971–1976).

Raimon Panikkar was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. After studies including Madrid and Lateran, he taught at Complutense University of Madrid (1946–1953), Harvard (1967–1971), and the University of California, Santa Barbara (1971–1978; emeritus ~1987–2010).

Raimond Gaita is a philosopher who studied at the University of Melbourne and University of Leeds. He served as Professor of Moral Philosophy at King's College London (1977–2011) and Foundation Professor of Philosophy at Australian Catholic University (1993–2011).

Raja Ram Shastri was a scholar in Indology. He served as a Member of the Lok Sabha (~1971–1977) and as Chairman of the Managing Committee at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University (attested 1976).

Rajan Gurukkal is a historian who completed degrees at the University of Calicut and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He served as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988) and Sundararajan Visiting Professor at the Indian Institute of Science (2012–2016).

Rajan Khatiwoda is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He worked as a Research Assistant and Cataloguer for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project (~2003–2013) and served as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica (~2014).
Rajanaka Mahes'vara was an Indologist. He served as Departmental Pandit (attested 1923) and Pandit (attested 1925) at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir.
Rajaram Hegde is a history, archaeology, and religious studies scholar. As of 2010, he served as Director at Kuvempu University and as Director of the Centre for the Study of Local Cultures.

Rajendra Chandra Hazra was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka under Sushil Kumar De. He taught at Jagannath University (1931), the University of Dhaka (1939–1951), and Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

Rajendralal Mitra was an Indologist and historian educated at Calcutta institutions. He served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and president (1885) of The Asiatic Society, and as director of Wards' Institution (1856–1881).

Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University. He held academic posts at Presidency University and Scottish Church College.
Raju Rimal is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who held posts at the National Archives of Nepal and served as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica (both attested 2018).

Rakhal Das Banerji was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Presidency and the University of Calcutta. He worked as an officer for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926) and held the Manindra Chandra Nandy professorship at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche studied under Gendun Chopel and Trijang Rinpoche.

Ralf Kramer is a Tibetology scholar who studied under David P. Jackson and earned an MA from the University of Hamburg. He served as Tibetan librarian at the Indian Institute, Oxford, and as Aris Librarian at the Bodleian Library (~2007).
